tspan.tspan: • Multiple parameters can change the time for a simulated disease to rebound
• Trajectories and points are colored according to a clustering algorithm based on
pre-supression dynamics, showing how similar diseases can rebound differently

text.tspan: • Acquired immunity has a different effect on time to rebound overall vs within

tspan.tspan: clusters, showing the complex role of different parameters on re-emergence
• Models can explain different re-emergence characteristics depending on
population dynamics, waning immunity, and seasonality
• These differing parameters correspond to different population dynamics of age-
dependent susceptibility, which drive outbreaks
• By quantifying uncertainty in the fits we will show what information on disease
spread has been gained by measuring rebounds
• In future these models could be deployed to understand which age groups drive
disease spread and anticipate disease rebounds after periods of supression
Benja
min J Singer
, Vennis Hong
, Joseph Lewnard
, Sara Tartof

Next steps for public health impact
• Kaiser Permanente Southern California data allows us to track respiratory
disease incidence using test-confirmed hospitalized cases

tspan.tspan: • After supression during the pandemic, each pathogen re-emerged differently
• Pathogen spread from other states helps
determine California outbreaks—we
modelled changes in spread using percent
positivity data and air travel
• Mobility data does not reliably translate
into infectious contact, so we fit a rough
stepwise model of contact changes,
capturing two major low-contact periods
